content: Tolazamide is an oral hypoglycemic medication that has been associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular mortality. It is essential to discuss the potential risks, benefits, and alternative treatments with your doctor before starting this medication. Tolazamide is prescribed to manage type 2 diabetes, a condition where the body does not use insulin effectively, leading to poor blood sugar control. It is particularly used in individuals whose diabetes cannot be managed by diet alone. This medication works by stimulating the pancreas to release insulin and improving the body’s ability to use insulin efficiently. However, for tolazamide to be effective, the pancreas must be capable of producing insulin. It is not suitable for treating type 1 diabetes, a condition where the body does not produce insulin at all. Tolazamide may also be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Tolazamide is available in tablet form and is typically taken once daily with breakfast. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency. Continue taking tolazamide even if you feel well, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. Before starting tolazamide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to tolazamide or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially antibiotics, anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), dexamethasone, diuretics, estrogens, isoniazid, MAO inhibitors, medications for high blood pressure or heart disease, niacin, oral contraceptives, phenytoin, prednisone, probenecid, and vitamins. Additionally, inform your doctor if you have or have had liver, kidney, thyroid, adrenal, heart, or pituitary disorders. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking tolazamide, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental procedures, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking tolazamide. Avoid unnecessary or prolonged exposure to sunlight, and use protective clothing, sunglasses, and sunscreen, as tolazamide may increase your skin’s sensitivity to sunlight. Follow all dietary and exercise recommendations provided by your doctor or dietitian. Maintain a healthy diet, and consult your doctor about the safe consumption of alcoholic beverages, as alcohol can lower blood sugar levels. If you miss a dose of tolazamide, take it as soon as you remember, unless it is almost time for your next dose. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Ask your doctor in advance what to do if you forget a dose, and write down these instructions for future reference. Tolazamide may cause changes in blood sugar levels. Be aware of the symptoms of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) and high blood sugar (hyperglycemia), and know how to respond if these occur. Symptoms of hypoglycemia include shakiness, dizziness, sweating, nervousness, irritability, sudden mood changes, headache, numbness or tingling around the mouth, weakness, pale skin, hunger, and clumsy or jerky movements. If you experience hypoglycemia, your doctor may advise you to check your blood sugar, consume a sugary food or drink (e.g., hard candy or fruit juice), or seek medical care. Severe hypoglycemia can lead to confusion, seizures, or loss of consciousness. Ensure that family, friends, and others around you are aware of these symptoms and know to seek immediate medical attention if they occur. Symptoms of hyperglycemia include extreme thirst, frequent urination, extreme hunger, weakness, and blurred vision. If untreated, hyperglycemia can lead to a life-threatening condition called diabetic ketoacidosis, characterized by dry mouth, upset stomach, vomiting, shortness of breath, fruity-smelling breath, and decreased consciousness. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience these symptoms. Tolazamide may cause side effects. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience a skin rash, itching, redness, exaggerated sunburn, yellowing of the skin or eyes, light-colored stools, dark urine, unusual bleeding or bruising, fever, or sore throat. Serious side effects should be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store tolazamide in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as regular tests will be required to monitor your response to tolazamide. Your doctor will also instruct you on how to check your blood or urine sugar levels at home. Always wear a diabetic identification bracelet to ensure proper treatment in emergencies. Do not share your medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
